title: UDLAP Document Extractor
subtitle: A browser tool the UDLAP IT department uses to turn stacks of scanned paperwork into clean spreadsheets.
about:
What is the UDLAP Document Extractor?

The IT department deals with thousands of paper documents a year: work orders, supply requests, maintenance logs. Someone had to type all of that into a spreadsheet by hand. The extractor is a web app that reads those scans with a vision model, pulls the fields, and exports everything to Excel. It runs in the browser, no backend to maintain.

challenge.title: The problem: paperwork at institutional scale
challenge.description: The documents are mixed formats, faded ink, handwritten notes, and no two forms look the same. Running them through a model one at a time wasn't going to cut it, and the API would rate-limit before the queue finished.

cards.title: No structure to lean on
cards.description: Scans have no metadata and no predictable layout. The model had to figure out the document type and the field positions from the image.

cards.title: Rate limits
cards.description: A long batch meant hitting the AI provider's cap. The app needed to pause, recover, and keep the browser responsive the whole time.

solution.title: The solution: a resilient browser pipeline
solution.description: A service manager runs the queue through a primary provider and falls back to a second one when the first fails. Everything is validated against a schema before it hits the UI.

features.title: Dual provider with fallback
features.description: Primary is Gemini Flash, fallback is Qwen-VL through OpenRouter. If one is down or rate-limited, the queue keeps moving.

features.title: Schema-enforced output
features.description: Responses are typed and validated at generation time, so hallucinated or malformed rows never make it into the sheet.

features.title: ZIP export
features.description: Processed files get renamed with their extracted context and bundled into a ZIP via JSZip, all client-side.

techStack.title: How it's built
techStack.description: React 19 on Vite. Everything runs in the browser with no server to maintain.

categories.name: Frontend
categories.description: React 19 and Vite, with TypeScript end to end.

categories.name: Vision models
categories.description: @google/genai for Gemini and the OpenRouter SDK for Qwen-VL. JSON schema mode is used to constrain outputs.

categories.name: Browser APIs
categories.description: Native File API, base64 encoding for the multimodal payload, and JSZip for the archive.

results.title: No more manual typing
results.description: What used to take hours per batch now takes a few minutes while the queue runs.

results.title: No server to run
results.description: Everything lives in the browser, which means the IT team doesn't have to maintain anything.

results.title: Keeps going when the API doesn't
results.description: The fallback provider keeps the batch moving when the primary gets rate-limited.
